target.title: fix(deploy): prove permanent Gitcrawl canary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A crawl-remote deployment can advertise Gitcrawl query support without proving that all six read-only query shapes work against deterministic data, that the live OpenClaw archive is fresh and complete, or that rolling propagation did not mix query responses from a predecessor release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Packages a checksum-pinned hidden canary seed into the immutable release artifact, seeds it only after exact deployment ownership and rollback-runtime proof, validates all six query envelopes and deterministic rows through the Access route, verifies fresh live coverage, and requires every query envelope to identify the exact deployed release. The permanent canary is intentionally retained across Worker rollback because the previously deployed runtime must declare canary support first.

## User Impact

Maintainers get deployment-time proof that hosted Gitcrawl queries are data-bearing, snapshot-consistent, release-consistent, hidden from archive listings, and backed by fresh complete live coverage before a crawl-remote release succeeds.

## Dependencies

- stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/550
- requires query-level release provenance from https://github.com/openclaw/crawl-remote/pull/40

## Evidence

- 28 focused deployment tests pass
- mixed predecessor-release query and live-coverage regressions are rejected
- checksum-pinned actionlint 1.7.12 passes
- focused `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, active-surface, and limits checks pass
- `limits.cpu_ms=300000` remains enforced
- canary SQL SHA-256: `d27e559bd5d96f9778b104583293ebaa314fa1b5af35bae268b0a928254263f4`
- no repair activation, action lifecycle modules, raw logs, or GitHub mutation added
